question.text: Among the following, the species that is both paramagnetic and coloured is:

solution.text: <math><msup><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup><mo>;</mo></math> Mn is in + 6 oxidation state. Electronic configuration is <math><msup><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>18</mn></mrow></msup><mn>3</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msup></math> . As it contains one unpaired electron it is paramagnetic and green coloured because of d-d transition in visible region. <math><msup><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are diamagnetic.
